topic: Bayes' Theorem and Independence: Unlocking Predictive Logic

sections.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: The Concept of Conditional Probability
lecture_lines: Conditional probability focuses on a smaller universe.
We shrink the space to event B.
Then, calculate the overlap with event A.
animations: Fade in Venn diagram representing A and B, color A #FF0000.
Animate reduction of sample space to B in blue (#0000FF).
Highlight intersection A and B in purple (#800080).
Label intersection as 'A and B' in yellow (#FFFF00).

sections.title: Independence: The 'No Influence' Rule
lecture_lines: Independence means events do not influence each other.
Knowing B tells us nothing about A.
Mathematically, P of A given B equals P of A.
animations: Show two independent events A and B as separate circles.
Fade out circle B to show A remains unchanged.

sections.title: The Core of Bayes' Theorem
lecture_lines: We predict the cause from observed evidence.
The result is a posterior probability.
animations: Animate sliding of terms to reveal Bayesian inversion structure.
Flash entire formula to emphasize the relationship.

sections.title: Synthesis: Independence vs. Dependency in Bayes
lecture_lines: When independent, the diagnostic power vanishes.
The formula reduces to the prior probability.
animations: Contrast independent case with dependent case visuals.
Use flow arrows to show influence direction in dependent case.
Fade out influence arrows to show independence.

sections.title: Conclusion and Application
lecture_lines: Bayes is the engine of modern AI.
Naive Bayes assumes features are independent.
It is efficient but sometimes less accurate.
animations: Highlight key takeaways in bold orange (#FFA500).
Fade out display to conclude section.
